sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum (record ad sales, record TV time share, 17% revenue growth) but the headline EPS miss due to a one-time Brazil tax charge and the absence of any formal 2026 guidance (deferred to January) leave forward expectations flat. Management's confident language ('feeling good about our growth trajectory') is not backed by a guidance raise, and the structural risk of the Brazil tax continuing (though small) and intensified live-sports competition are noted. The net effect is a mixed read with no clear change in forward expectations, anchoring the score at 0.0.

summary.eps: $5.87 versus roughly $6.96 consensus, an optical miss attributable to the Brazil charge.
summary.guidance: No full-year 2026 guidance given, deferred to the January call. No 2026 advertising revenue guidance provided. Management expressed confidence: 'feeling good about our growth trajectory' and 'a pretty great 2026 coming up after this phenomenal Q4.'
summary.margin: Operating margin 28%, down from 30% a year earlier and below the 31.5% guidance, driven by a $619M Brazil tax expense.
key_risks: The EPS/margin miss itself, even if one-time.
Brazil Supreme Court ruled against Netflix 7–4 on the tax scope; the tax is now a permanent cost of doing business in Brazil.
No 2026 numbers on the table yet, with the market asked to wait until January.
Intensifying live-sports competition (Apple F1, Paramount UFC).
WBD / Warner Bros. acquisition rumours in the background (regulatory and execution overhang).
key_opportunities: Best ad-sales quarter ever, on track to more than double ad revenue in 2025.
Record share of TV time in Q3 in both the US (8.6%) and the UK (9.4%).
Total view hours grew a bit faster in Q3 2025 than in H1 2025.
Canelo-Crawford fight drew 41M+ live viewers and ranked top 10 in 91 countries.
Approaching 1 billion people globally for programming, still only ~7% of addressable consumer-spend market and ~10% of TV time in biggest markets.
